grandparents_cupboard.reason: Fruit, flour, oats, hazelnuts, sugar, oil and cinnamon are all plain home-kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: Only a baking dish, a bowl, a knife and a grater or zester are needed, and rubbing in a crumble is beginner technique.

works.reason: Three oranges and two Bramleys under a 215g oat and hazelnut topping, baked at 190°C for 30 to 35 minutes, gives a sensible crumble for four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers zesting and peeling the oranges, peeling and slicing the apples, chopping the nuts and rubbing the topping, and the 35-minute cook time matches the bake.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon appear in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm crumble suits a chilly late-March afternoon, and the oranges lead the filling and the title alongside stored Bramleys.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with no fuss.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is mostly fruit, oats and nuts with modest added sugar, a real-food treat a family would happily make again.
